title: Indirect Control of Buried CoB Spin Textures via C$_{60}$-Induced Modification of Ir Spin-Orbit Coupling
authors: Colin Kirkbride, Christopher E A Barker, Timothy Moorsom, Kayla Fallon, Daniel Roe, Trevor Almeida, Sara Villa, Christopher H Marrows, Stephen McVitie
abstract: Understanding how organic materials modulate magnetic structure is a central challenge in organic spintronics. Here, we demonstrate that C$_{60}$ molecular films exert a pronounced and quantifiable influence on the buried magnetic spin texture in Pt/CoB/Ir based multilayer systems hosting interfacial Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (iDMI). Using Lorentz transmission electron microscopy, the magnetic domain behaviour in field-free and in-situ field environments is measured. In Fresnel mode, we reveal a reduction in magnetic domain periodicity upon C$_{60}$ deposition. Then, using pixelated 4D-STEM differential phase contrast mode, we establish that this modification arises from a substantial enhancement of effective magnetic anisotropy and interfacial DMI strength. Coupled with bulk magnetometry and micromagnetic simulations, we propose a mechanism based on spin-orbit coupling at the C$_{60}$/Ir interface which modifies the iDMI and drives a contraction of spin texture density throughout the multilayer stack. These findings extend the impact of organic molecular capping films as effective and accessible routes for engineering spin textures to buried magnetic multilayer systems, with direct implications for the design of next-generation spintronic and neuromorphic devices.
summary: This work demonstrates that depositing C60 molecular films can act as an effective, non-hybridizing gate to control the magnetic spin textures in buried metallic multilayers. By enhancing the interfacial Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya Interaction (iDMI) through spin-orbit coupling at the C60/Ir interface, the C60 layer causes a measurable contraction of the magnetic domain period. This offers a promising route for designing next-generation spintronic devices.
main_problem: The study addresses how organic molecules, specifically C60 films, can indirectly modulate the magnetic spin texture buried within metallic multilayer systems.
main_result: C60 deposition significantly reduces the magnetic domain periodicity by enhancing the effective magnetic anisotropy and the interfacial Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya Interaction (iDMI).
method: The research combines advanced experimental techniques like Lorentz TEM and STEM-DPC with theoretical tools such as micromagnetic simulations and effective medium models.
model_or_system: The physical system is a multilayer stack, typically Pt/CoB/Ir, where the magnetic properties are controlled by the introduction of a C60 molecular capping layer.
key_observables: Magnetic domain periodicity, domain wall widths, effective magnetic anisotropy (K_eff), and interfacial DMI strength (|D|).
important_parameters: The influence of C60-induced modification of spin-orbit coupling (SOC) at the C60/Ir interface.
main_assumptions: The mechanism relies on the C60 modifying the iDMI via SOC, and simulations use an effective medium model.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the full stack structure and atomic columns, while measurements compare domain periods and wall widths between C60-capped and Pt-capped samples.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem of organic modulation of magnetism, presents experimental measurements comparing C60 vs. Pt capping, derives enhanced magnetic parameters (K_eff, DMI) for the C60 case, and concludes with a proposed SOC-mediated mechanism.
why_interesting: While focused on magnetism, the concept of using molecular interfaces to tune fundamental quantum interactions like DMI via SOC provides a model for engineering quantum materials interfaces.
